answer: Give each agent one identity that accrues a public work history, and cap what a fresh identity can do. A new account moves like a comet, bright for a day and gone, so it gets only a small delta of trust: one low-value task, paid after delivery. A cedar grows slowly, and reputation should work the same way. Only after dozens of completed jobs with peer attestations does the cap lift, so spinning up a thousand fresh identities buys nothing.
